children: on Sunday introduced Allia Celeo, a ceiling-mounted medical imaging system designed for cardiac and other minimally invasive procedures, at the Transcatheter Cardiovascular Therapeutics conference in San Diego.

The system combines artificial intelligence-assisted imaging, automated equipment positioning and remote monitoring technology to help clinicians perform procedures involving blood vessels, the heart and other organs.
For investors, the introduction expands GE HealthCare's
portfolio of interventional imaging equipment as hospitals seek to improve procedure efficiency and manage operating costs.

Allia Celeo features a wide-opening C-arm, an X-ray imaging device that rotates around patients to capture images from different angles. Its ceiling-mounted design provides additional space for medical staff and equipment, while automated positioning aims to reduce interruptions during procedures.
AI-enabled software adjusts imaging settings to balance image quality and radiation exposure. A digital representation of the equipment helps clinicians preview positioning before making adjustments.

software used to visualize coronary stents, guide heart valve procedures and assist with cancer treatments. It also works with OnWatch Predict, which uses remote monitoring and predictive analytics to identify potential equipment problems before breakdowns occur.
Allia Celeo follows the introduction of the floor-mounted Allia Moveo in 2025, which became commercially available earlier this year.
